x: Further down the field were rivals Eamonn Martin and Ian Hamer. Darrin Morris was 6th in the discus, 54.06, and John Regis found himself shunted back to 4th in the short sprint in 10.52 with Lennie Paul 6th, 10.56.

What can I say about Paul Evans - second fastest time of the day with 23:55 behind Eamonn Martin's 23:45. Paul's coach, John Bicourt, told me that Paul would only be running easy before his attempt in the London Marathon the following week.

With three laps to go Richard Nerurkar, Britain's 10k hero of last year's World Champs., threw in a 63 second lap in an attempt to shake off the ever threatening Eamonn Martin and Paul was unable to handle the increase in tempo.
In windy conditions Paul Evans ran to the fastest 10k by a Briton since Eamonn Martin's British record in 1988. Several star Kenyans were behind him and Gary Staines's club record went by 41/100ths.

Once again Basildon's Eamonn Martin was way out of it when it mattered. Three days later it was even hotter for the final (31C/41%) and the Belgravian won the admiration of many a British distance runner as, with no thought of running a "safe" race, he got stuck into the pack to do some damage while he could.

Belgrave Harriers have arrived in Shepway and in Kent, and our hand of friendship goes out to all fellow athletes in other clubs, but look out on the track, these young Belgravians are coming. Left: The young man who started it all, Nigel Whorlow, receives an award from Eamonn Martin

Gary Staines was there to act as pace-maker for Eamon Martin and at Tower Bridge was leading a very large pack which included a slightly unhappy looking Paul Evans and about a minute further back was Kassa Tadesse.
Basildon's Eamonn Martin was the class act of the day. Churning out the laps in the 5k, it seemed for some time that he was destined to crack the league record.
Gary's start was more conservative and by Tower Bridge he was conspicuous in the second wave of international runners with former winner Eamonn Martin already struggling just ahead.

The race was an absolute treat for Belgrave supporters glued to the television as a small but elite group broke away from the masses and included Masya, the Spaniard Antonio Serrano, Basildon's Eamonn Martin and Rob Denmark and the Belgrave trio of Evans, Staines and Kassa Tadesse.

Basildon's Eamonn Martin and Gary Staines dropped away as only the American Lawson joined Evans in clinging on to the Russian's tail. A 25 metre gap opened at one point but at 18 miles three consecutive sub-4:50s put Evans in the clear.
